authoredFrom: SOL-25 — member resolution: receiver-typed members and implicit-`this` inherited calls, WITH the project index. Authored 2026-10-28 from the analyzer's measured output on this directory.
note: This subdirectory is a project: `sol25-lib.sol` declares two libraries that both declare `shared`, and two contracts that both declare `inherited`. The four POSITIVE rows show the two mechanisms (`receiverTypedMember`, `inheritedMemberQualified`); the three NEGATIVE rows are the guards, and each is a row the pass must leave alone: a name ONE type declares (the bare spelling already resolves), a declarer that is the enclosing type's OWN override, and a receiver name declared with TWO types in one file. A fixture that only pinned the rewrites would pass a pass that rewrote everything.

expectRelationships.comment: The receiver is declared `Lib.T`; `Lib` declares `shared` and `Lib2` declares it too, so the bare name is ambiguous project-wide and the declared type determines the declarer. The target is the declaration's own qualifiedName, which is what the arbiter's key space carries.
Same evidence through a STATE variable, not a parameter — the declared-type map covers both.

A BARE callee. `inherited` is declared by BaseA and BaseZ, so the name collides; Child's inheritance closure names BaseA as the one declarer. This row also pins the classifier fix: before it, a bare call whose name any sibling type declared was labelled `inFileTypeMember` and never reached the cross-file branch.
CONTROL — `unique` is declared by ONE project type, so the bare spelling already names one declaration. The pass must not rewrite it: a qualified spelling can collide where the bare one did not.
NEGATIVE — `Both` overrides `inherited` itself, so the declarer IS the enclosing type. There is no ancestor to qualify to, and the row keeps its bare target.

NEGATIVE — the name `dup` is declared with `Lib.T` (state) and `Lib2.T` (parameter) in this one file. The receiver's type is not a fact about the site, so the target stays bare: a candidate is not a resolution.
The call site itself spells the library; the object has ONE project declaration and its closure declares `min`, so the qualified target is what the source says.

NEGATIVE for the static rule and POSITIVE for the receiver rule in one row: a state variable named `Lib` shadows the library, so the object is a VALUE. The static branch must not fire (it would have published `Lib.shared`, naming a library the call does not use) and the receiver branch resolves the declared type instead.

The receiver is an ELEMENT of a mapping (`mapping(bytes32 => Lib.T) _byKey`), so there is no declared variable to type — the container's VALUE TYPE names it. `calleeObject` is empty on this shape (the object is `_byKey[k]`), so the container name travels as `calleeObjectBase`.

The source states the receiver's type: `IThing(a).ping(1)`. The grammar fills no `function` field for a conversion, so the type is read as the call's FIRST named child — the field-only read returned "" and left these rows unresolved.

An applied modifier declared on a base in ANOTHER file, with the same name declared by a second type: the enclosing type's closure names BaseA, and the qualified spelling is one key. The edge now carries `decoratesOwner`, which it had no field for before.

forbidRelationships.comment: The implicit-`this` row must NOT keep its bare spelling — that is the whole movement.
The two-type receiver must not be resolved to EITHER candidate.
…including the one whose name the parameter's declared type heads.
An override call must not be qualified to an ancestor — it names the enclosing type's own declaration.
The single-declarer control must not be rewritten at all.
The static call must not keep its bare spelling.
A shadowing VALUE must not be read as the library of the same name.
An indexed element must not keep the bare member spelling.
A conversion receiver's member must not keep the bare spelling: the type is written in the call.
The inherited modifier must not keep its bare spelling.
